newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT-Schaeffer goes neutral on US stocks.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Schaeffer goes neutral on US stocks.

text.p: Well known U.S. market analyst Bernie Schaeffer, who runs the Investment Research Institute in Cincinnati, turned neutral on U.S. stocks and bonds from bullish, the firm said Friday.

"In the near term, we do not anticipate a major bullish reversal of the recent bond market selloff, which began August 1 and accelerated today," Investment Research analyst Moby Waller said in a report.
He said September U.S. Treasury bond futures have moved lower since forming a double top around the 115 level. They fell 1-17/32 to 112-22/32 on Friday.
Waller said the expected lack of a rebound in bonds will likely hinder stock gains over the near term.
The bellwether Dow industrial average .DJI dropped 157 points to 8,031 Friday after losing 71 points Thursday.
Waller added that bullish sentiment in both bonds and stocks, as measured by Consensus Inc, was very high.
"A further short term concern for stocks has been the renewed interest in beaten-down technology shares," Waller said in the report.
